passages.original: adjutorem sibi Deum, et assiduum adjuto- rem, nec illi sufficit assiduum, sed nc aliquando illum despiciat, orationibus pronus exoptat; et per corpus omne psalterii boc et praedicat et clamat. Si ergo boc ille ita h magnus scit ut assidue dicere, ita necessa- rium confessus est, ut doceret : quemadmodum Pelagius Coelestiusque seposita omni responsione psalmorum, talique abdicata doctrina, suasuros se aliquibus esse contidunt, nos adjutorium Dei nec debere quaerere, nec egere; cum omnes sancti ni- hil se sine hoc agere posse testentur?
passages.english: [he asks for] God as his helper, and a constant helper; nor is "constant" enough for him, but bowed in prayer he longs that [God] may never at any time despise him; and throughout the whole body of the Psalter he both proclaims and cries out this. If, then, so great a man knows this so well that he says it constantly, and has confessed it to be so necessary that he taught it, how is it that Pelagius and Caelestius, setting aside every answer of the psalms and renouncing such teaching, are confident that they will persuade some people that we neither ought to seek God's help nor need it, when all the saints testify that they can do nothing without it?
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence; the governing verb (perhaps 'he asks for' or 'he invokes') falls in the preceding text. Scanning errors corrected: 'boc' for 'hoc', 'nc' for 'ne', 'contidunt' for 'confidunt'; the stray 'h' is a footnote mark. The rhetorical question is introduced by 'quemadmodum' ('how'), which reads awkwardly in the Latin; it has been rendered as 'how is it that'.

passages.original: 1. In his, teste Augustino ( Lib. de Gratia Christi, c. 50), Pelagius dicit, esse de quibus eum homines infamare conantur : unum, quod neget parvulis baptismi sacramentum, et absque redemptione Christi aliquibus coelorum regna promittat : aliud, quod ita dicat posse hominem vitare peccatum, ut Dei excludat auxilium, et in tantum libero confidat arbitrio, ut gratiae repudiet adjutorium.
passages.english: 1. Among these, as Augustine testifies (On the Grace of Christ, ch. 50), Pelagius says there are [two things] about which people try to defame him: one, that he denies the sacrament of baptism to infants, and promises the kingdom of heaven to some without the redemption of Christ; the other, that he says a man is able to avoid sin in such a way that he excludes the help of God, and trusts in free will to such an extent that he rejects the aid of grace.
passages.notes: The Latin 'In his' ('Among these') refers to matters outside the passage.

passages.original: 3. Deinde, inquit Augustinus (Ibid.), cum de homi- nis conditione, et ad peccandum atque non peccandum naturali ejus possibilitate quaedam interposuisset, ad-junxit : Quam liberi arbitrii potestatem dicimus in omnibus esse generaliter, in Christianis, in Judaeis atque Gentilibus. In omnibus est liberum arbitrium aequaliter per naturam : sed in solis Christianis ju- vatur a gratia. In illis nudum et inerme est condi- tionis bonum : in his vero qui ad Christum perti- nent, Christi munitur auxilio.
passages.english: 3. Then, says Augustine (Ibid.), after he had inserted certain remarks on the condition of man and on his natural capacity both for sinning and for not sinning, he added: "This power of free choice we say is present generally in all, in Christians, in Jews and in Gentiles. In all, free choice is present equally by nature; but in Christians alone it is helped by grace. In the former the good of [their] condition is bare and unarmed; but in those who belong to Christ it is fortified by Christ's help."
passages.notes: The speaker quoted by Augustine is evidently Pelagius (cf. Augustine, De gratia Christi), though he is not named in the passage.

passages.original: Is porro fidei liber totus insertus Sermoni alias Au- gustini de Tempore 191, nunc append. 236, n. 2 et seqq. ac praeterca seorsim editus est in appendice to. x novae editionis ejusdem sancti, pag. 96, sicut et apud Hieronymum, cui olim ascriptus fuerat.
passages.english: This book of faith, moreover, was inserted in its entirety into what was formerly Sermon 191 of Augustine's De Tempore, now Appendix [Sermon] 236, no. 2 and following; and it has also been published separately in the appendix of volume 10 of the new edition of the same saint, page 96, as [it has been] also among [the works of] Jerome, to whom it had once been ascribed.
passages.notes: 'praeterca' read as 'praeterea'. The 'book of faith' is Pelagius' Libellus fidei, once attributed to Jerome and inserted among Augustine's sermons.
